stem: A new order-processing service needs several EC2 instances to concurrently mount and write to the same filesystem of generated output files. Which storage choice satisfies this requirement?

choices.text: An Amazon EBS volume attached to one of the instances
Amazon EFS, mounted concurrently by every instance that needs the shared files
Amazon S3 accessed through its API from each instance
Instance store volumes physically attached to each individual instance's host

rationale: Amazon EFS is a shared, network-mounted filesystem that many instances can mount concurrently, which is exactly the multi-instance, same-filesystem requirement stated. An EBS volume attaches to a single EC2 instance at a time, so it cannot be the shared, concurrently mounted filesystem multiple instances need. Amazon S3 is accessed through an API rather than mounted as a filesystem, so instances that need actual filesystem semantics for shared output files cannot use it as stated. Instance store volumes are physically attached to one host and are not shared across instances at all, and the data on them is lost whenever that instance stops or terminates, so it fails both the sharing and durability parts of the requirement.
